blocks.content: A liveness probe checks whether a container is still functioning correctly, if it fails repeatedly, kubelet kills and restarts the container, exactly the self-healing mechanism covered in the ReplicaSet & Replication module, now triggered by an active health check rather than a crash.

A liveness probe is a repeated, active check, an HTTP request, a TCP connection attempt, or a command run inside the container, verifying the application inside is genuinely still functioning, not just that its process happens to still exist.

blocks.alt: An active, ongoing check of genuine functionality, not just process existence

blocks.content: When a liveness probe fails enough times in a row, kubelet kills the container and starts a fresh one, exactly the same replacement mechanism covered in the Pod Replacement topic, just triggered by a failed health check instead of a crash.

blocks.alt: The same replacement mechanism, now triggered by a health check, not a crash

blocks.content: This is exactly why liveness probes matter beyond simple process monitoring: a genuinely deadlocked or stuck process is still technically running, its process has not exited, but it is completely unresponsive, only an active health check like this can catch that.

blocks.alt: A stuck, unresponsive process, invisible to anything just checking "is it running"

blocks.content: A liveness probe can be an HTTP GET request (checking for a successful status code), a raw TCP connection attempt (just checking the port accepts connections), or an exec command run inside the container (checking its exit code), chosen based on what actually makes sense for the application.

blocks.alt: Three probe mechanisms, chosen to fit what the application can actually expose

blocks.content: An HTTP-based liveness probe hitting a dedicated /healthz endpoint is a common, practical pattern, the endpoint itself simply confirms the application's core logic is still responsive.

blocks.alt: A dedicated, lightweight health endpoint, purpose-built for exactly this check

blocks.content:
livenessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /healthz
    port: 8080
  initialDelaySeconds: 10
  periodSeconds: 10

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: A liveness probe actively checks whether a container is genuinely functioning, not just running, repeated failures trigger a real container restart.
It exists specifically to catch deadlocked or stuck processes that a simple "is the process alive" check would completely miss.
